question: What is the primary focus of disease surveillance compared to clinical diagnosis?

options.A: The health status of the entire population
options.B: The pharmacological efficacy of a specific drug
options.C: The financial auditing of a health facility
options.D: The physiological recovery of a single patient

explanation: Surveillance is a population-level activity aimed at tracking community health trends rather than diagnosing individual illnesses. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why is disease surveillance described as an ongoing and systematic process?

options.A: It requires daily physical examinations of every citizen in the country
options.B: It relies on continuous data gathering rather than sporadic or one-off surveys
options.C: It replaces the need for standard clinical record keeping in hospitals
options.D: It is only performed when a major epidemic has already broken out

explanation: Continuous collection allows health systems to establish baseline disease patterns and spot sudden deviations immediately. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: What is the ultimate aim of public health surveillance?

options.A: To replace clinical doctors with data analysts
options.B: To reduce morbidity and mortality through timely action
options.C: To increase health insurance enrollment nationwide
options.D: To publish academic research papers for universities

explanation: All data collection ultimately serves the practical goal of preventing disease spread and saving lives. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: How does surveillance assist in evaluating public health interventions?

options.A: By calculating the exact salary needed for community health workers
options.B: By testing the purity of drinking water sources in urban centers
options.C: By determining which hospital rooms require structural repairs
options.D: By showing whether disease rates drop following a vaccination campaign

explanation: Tracking disease incidence before and after an intervention reveals whether the program achieved its intended protective effect. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: Which type of surveillance relies on health workers making regular visits to facilities to actively search for cases?
explanation: Active surveillance requires public health staff to proactively seek out cases rather than waiting for reports to arrive. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of syndromic surveillance over traditional laboratory-confirmed surveillance?

options.A: It is completely free to implement across all levels of government
options.B: It eliminates the need for any community health education programs
options.C: It guarantees 100 percent diagnostic accuracy for every single patient
options.D: It detects potential outbreaks earlier by tracking symptoms before lab results are ready

explanation: By monitoring clinical signs and symptoms instantly, syndromic systems bypass delays inherent in laboratory testing. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What are the three core epidemiological variables used when analyzing surveillance data?
explanation: Epidemiological analysis breaks down disease occurrence by when it happened, where it occurred, and who was affected. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why is the dissemination of analyzed data back to healthcare workers considered a critical step in the surveillance loop?

options.A: It fulfills a legal requirement for international travel clearances
options.B: It ensures that hospital pharmacies maintain a surplus of expensive drugs
options.C: It prevents patients from seeking care at private clinics
options.D: It empowers frontline clinicians to understand local trends and act on them

explanation: Feedback reports inform frontline staff about circulating pathogens, encouraging vigilance and appropriate clinical management. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Which agency coordinates the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response strategy in Nigeria?

options.B: National Primary Health Care Development Agency
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration

explanation: The NCDC serves as the apex public health agency responsible for leading disease surveillance and outbreak response in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: At which administrative tier does formal disease reporting typically begin in the Nigerian healthcare structure?

options.D: Primary healthcare facility and LGA level

explanation: Data collection starts at the grassroot primary care level before being collated and transmitted through the Local Government Area office. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: What triggers an immediate public health outbreak investigation?

options.A: An unusual cluster of cases detected through surveillance data
options.B: A request from international tourism agencies
options.C: The retirement of a senior hospital medical director
options.D: The annual routine budgeting cycle of the ministry of health

explanation: Surveillance aberrations—such as cases exceeding expected seasonal baselines—serve as the primary trigger for field investigations. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why is contact tracing an essential component of outbreak response for infectious diseases?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory testing of clinical blood samples
options.B: It guarantees that the outbreak will never recur in the same community
options.C: It provides accurate financial compensation for families affected by illness
options.D: It helps identify individuals who may have been exposed so they can be monitored or treated

explanation: Tracing contacts breaks the transmission chain by isolating and monitoring people before they spread the pathogen further. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why are community health nurses uniquely positioned for disease surveillance?

options.A: They are solely responsible for funding public health budgets
options.B: They spend most of their working hours analyzing data in central laboratories
options.C: They possess exclusive authority to declare national states of emergency
options.D: They have direct, regular contact with patients and families at the grassroots level

explanation: Daily clinical encounters place nurses at the ideal vantage point to spot unusual health events early. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: Which of the following tasks is a direct nursing responsibility within a surveillance system?

options.A: Reporting notifiable diseases and collecting diagnostic specimens
options.B: Designing software algorithms for national database servers
options.C: Enforcing quarantine laws through judicial court orders
options.D: Importing vaccines from international manufacturing plants

explanation: Frontline nurses routinely identify notifiable conditions, complete reporting paperwork, and safely gather clinical samples. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge facing surveillance systems in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Excessive financial surplus and overfunded health budgets
options.C: Shortages of trained public health personnel
options.D: Delayed reporting and poor internet connectivity

explanation: Resource-limited settings typically struggle with underfunding rather than having excessive financial surpluses. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h8)

question: How do electronic disease surveillance systems (eIDSR) improve upon paper-based reporting?

options.A: They make laboratory confirmation completely unnecessary
options.B: They eliminate the need for any healthcare workers in rural areas
options.C: They ensure that diseases never occur in rural communities again
options.D: They speed up data transmission and reduce human transcription errors

explanation: Digital platforms transmit data instantly from remote sites to central databases while minimizing manual paperwork mistakes. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h8)
